Master layers Objects on a master layer appear on every page, under the page's own layers: use them for a logo, a header or page numbers. Click the New Master Layer (All Pages); right-click for odd or even pages button to add one for all pages; right-click it to add one for odd or even pages only. A master layer's menu has Show on to choose All pages, Odd pages or Even pages. You can select and edit master objects from any page they show on. Renaming objects and layers Double-click a layer or an object in the panel, or choose Rename from its menu, to open the Rename Layer or Rename Object dialog box. Type the new name and click OK. An object with an empty name shows what it is again. Double-click the page row to rename the page.  Names help you find objects in the panel and in Find and replace, and are kept in exported SVG files. Changing the order Object > Order moves the selected objects: To Front of Page, To Back of Page, To Front of Layer, To Back of Layer, Forward One, Back One, In Front Of, Behind (click the object to go in front of or behind) and Reverse Order. Grouping and combining Object > Group > Group (Ctrl+G) makes the selection one group that moves and resizes together. Ungroup (Ctrl+U) splits it again, and Ungroup All also splits the groups inside it. To edit an object inside a group without ungrouping, Ctrl+click it. Combine (Ctrl+L) makes the selected objects one curve of several parts, with one fill and outline; where the parts overlap, holes appear. Break Apart (Ctrl+K) splits a curve into its parts. Convert to Curves (Ctrl+Q) turns a rectangle, ellipse, polygon or text into a curve you can edit node by node. Locking and hiding objects Object > Lock > Lock Object keeps the selected objects from being selected or changed; Unlock Object and Unlock All Objects release them. Object > Hide > Hide Object hides the selected objects; Show All Objects shows them again. To keep objects out of the way while you work on others, see also Focus mode.

h: With objects selected With nothing selected
x: The Properties panel The Properties panel (Alt+Enter) shows and changes the properties of the selected objects: their outline, fill, transparency and more, depending on what is selected. It is open at first, beside Hints and Objects. Open it again with Object > Properties.  With objects selected The top of the panel names the selected object (and how many more are selected) and gives its position and size. Under it, a row of buttons opens and closes each section the object has: QR code, for a QR code: its content and look; see Barcodes and QR codes. Outline: color, width, paint, caps, corners, dashes, arrowheads and more; see Setting outlines. Fill: the kind of fill and its settings; see Fills. F11 opens this section. Transparency: how much of what lies below shows through; see Transparency. Rectangle, for rectangles: the corner settings; see Corners. FX: the bitmap effects applied to the object; see Bitmap effects. Character, for text: the font, size, Bold and Italic, and a button to Edit with the Text tool (F8). Summary: a summary of the object. The sections you closed stay closed the next time. A change applies to every selected object and is one undo step. With nothing selected With nothing selected, the panel says No objects selected and shows the Default properties for new objects: the fill and outline that new shapes and lines get. Change them here to draw with other colors from the start. See Object styles and defaults.

h: To place objects inside a frame Editing what is inside Opacity masks Empty frames
x: Placing objects inside a frame A clip frame is a closed object that holds other objects and shows only the parts of them that lie inside it, like a picture in a window. The frame keeps its own fill and outline; the objects inside stay whole and can be taken out again. The commands are in Object > Clip to Frame. To place objects inside a frame Select the objects to place inside. Choose Object > Clip to Frame > Place Inside Frame. Click the closed object that will be the frame. The objects keep their position. You can also drag the objects onto the frame with the right mouse button and choose to place them inside; see Dragging with the right button. Editing what is inside Edit Contents enters the frame: only the objects inside can be edited, the rest of the page is dimmed and the frame shows as an outline. Finish Editing Contents, or the button on the property bar, leaves it. Extract Contents makes the objects inside ordinary objects again; the frame stays, empty. Lock Contents to Frame (on at first): moving, scaling or rotating the frame takes the contents along. Turned off, the frame moves alone and the contents stay where they are on the page. Double-clicking a frame with the Pick tool also enters it; see Focus mode. Opacity masks Object > Clip to Frame > Opacity Mask turns the selected clip frames into opacity masks: the frame is no longer drawn, and its brightness decides how much of the contents shows: fully where it is white, not at all where it is black, and nothing outside the frame. Fill the frame with a gradient for a soft fade. Invert Mask swaps that, so black shows. Choose the command again to turn the mask back into a plain frame. Empty frames Right-click an object and use its frame type commands: Create empty clip frame turns each selected object into an empty clip frame, ready to hold objects. No frame turns an empty clip frame back into the object it was. Create empty text frame replaces the object by an empty paragraph text frame of its size, ready for the Text tool. Cropping a bitmap with the Crop tool or the Shape tool also places it in a clip frame; see Cropping, cutting and erasing.

h: To create a symmetry Editing a symmetry Removing or keeping the copies
x: Drawing with symmetry Symmetry draws live mirrored copies of an object across one or more mirror lines. The copies follow every change you make to the original, so you draw one half (or one slice) and see the whole. The commands are in Object > Symmetry. To create a symmetry Select an object. Choose Object > Symmetry > Create New Symmetry (Alt+S). A vertical mirror line is placed at the right edge of the object, so the copy appears next to it, and TraceDraw goes straight into editing the symmetry. Editing a symmetry Edit Symmetry (Alt+E) edits the symmetry of the selected object. A bar at the top left of the drawing window sets: the number of mirror lines, 1 to 12, spread evenly around the center. With more lines you get a kaleidoscope: with n lines there are 2*n* - 1 copies; the center (X and Y); the angle of the first line (0 to 360 degrees); Show full preview (copies drawn in full, or as red outlines when off) and Show symmetry lines. Edit the originals as usual, with any tool; the copies follow. A click or a marquee picks one of the originals inside the symmetry, and objects you draw, paste or duplicate join it. Drag a mirror line with the Pick tool to move the lines; click a line to show round handles at its ends and drag one to turn the lines. While an object with symmetry is selected or edited, its mirror lines show as dashed lines. Click Finish on the bar, or choose Finish Editing Symmetry (Alt+Shift+E), to stop editing. Removing or keeping the copies Remove Symmetry (Alt+Shift+S) removes the symmetry; the copies go away. Break Symmetry Link (Alt+X) turns the copies into objects of their own, which no longer follow the original.

h: Entering and leaving focus mode While in focus mode Settings
x: Focus mode Focus mode lets you edit the objects inside a group or a clip frame without ungrouping it, with the rest of the drawing faded behind it. Entering and leaving focus mode Double-click a group or a clip frame with the Pick tool. Or right-click an object and choose Bring into focus. For an object inside a group, the group gets the focus and the object stays selected. Double-click a group inside the focused group to go one level deeper. Press Esc with nothing selected to go up one level, and leave focus mode from the top. The cross on the breadcrumb bar leaves at once. While in focus mode A bar at the top left of the drawing window shows the name of the drawing, then each group on the way down. Click a step to go back to that group, or the name of the drawing to leave focus mode. Clicks and marquees select the objects inside the focused group, so you can move, color or delete them with the Pick tool as usual. Everything else is faded. Exports and printing are not affected. Settings How faded the other objects are is set by the visibility of inactive objects (0 to 100%, 20% at first) on the Edit page of Tools > Options > TraceDraw. Whether a double-click enters focus mode is set on the same page. See TraceDraw options.

h: Making a symbol Placing instances Turning instances back into objects
x: Symbols A symbol is an object you define once and place many times. Each copy, called an instance, is a link to the definition: edit the definition and every instance changes. Symbols keep files small and repeated parts the same. They are listed in the Symbols panel (Ctrl+F3).  Making a symbol Select the objects that make up the symbol. Click New symbol from selection in the Symbols panel, or choose Object > Symbol > New Symbol or Object > Create > Symbol. The selection becomes the first instance of the new symbol. Placing instances The panel lists the symbols of the drawing, each with the number of its instances. Click Insert beside a symbol to place a new instance, or choose Object > Symbol > Insert Symbol. Instances can be moved, scaled and turned like any object. Turning instances back into objects Select instances and click Revert to objects, or choose Object > Symbol > Revert to Objects. They become ordinary objects that no longer follow the symbol.

h: Adding and editing data
x: Object data The Object Data panel attaches your own information to an object, as named fields: a part number, a price, a note. The data is saved with the drawing and goes with the object when you copy it.  Adding and editing data Select an object. With nothing selected, the panel says Select an object.. The panel lists the object's fields in two columns, Field and Value. Click a name or a value to edit it. Click Add field to add a field, or one of the buttons for a common field: Name, Cost, Comments and CDRStaticID. Click the x at the end of a row to remove the field. When the selected objects have a Cost field with a number, the panel shows their total cost. Some features keep their own data in objects, such as dimension lines, callouts, connectors and anchors; you rarely need to change those fields by hand.

h: To add a link Bookmarks Links in exported files
x: Links and bookmarks The Links and Bookmarks panel gives objects a hyperlink, so a click on them in an exported PDF, SVG or web page opens a web address, writes an email or goes to another page. It also lists the named objects of the drawing as bookmarks. Open it from Window > Panels.  To add a link Select one or more objects. Type the address in the Hyperlink field and leave the field. The buttons Web, E-mail and Page put https://, mailto: or #page= in front of the text, so for a page link you only type its number. Click Remove to take a link away, or empty the field. Bookmarks Under Bookmarks (named objects), the panel lists one button per object that has a name. Click one to select the object and zoom to it. To name objects, see Renaming objects and layers. Links in exported files In PDF files, each linked object becomes a clickable area over its box. A page link goes to the top of that page of the file. PDF/X files get no links, as those standards do not allow them. In SVG and web pages, the object itself is the link. A link on a group covers all its objects; the links of the objects inside are left out.

h: To paste in another form
x: Paste Special Edit > Paste Special chooses how the content of the clipboard comes into the drawing, when it could come in more than one way: for example text copied from another program can become a text object, and an SVG copied from a web page can become editable shapes or a picture.  To paste in another form Copy something, in TraceDraw or in another program. Choose Edit > Paste Special. Under Paste as, choose one of the forms the clipboard offers: Objects (internal clipboard): objects copied in TraceDraw, as they were; Vector objects (SVG text): SVG text, turned into shapes you can edit; Bitmap: an image, as a bitmap; Artistic text: plain text, as a line of text. Click OK. When the clipboard holds nothing that can be pasted, the dialog box says The clipboard is empty. The ordinary Paste (Ctrl+V) pastes in the first form available, and Paste in View (Ctrl+Shift+V) pastes in the middle of the window.

h: Adding to the Shelf Placing an item Arranging items Removing an item Where the Shelf is kept
x: The Shelf The Shelf panel keeps objects and colors apart from any drawing, so you can place them in this drawing or another one, today or after TraceDraw restarts: logos, stamps, frames, a set of colors. Open it from Window > Panels, or right-click a selection and choose Add to Shelf.  Adding to the Shelf Select objects and click Add Selection. The item is named after the object (its name, or what it is), or "n objects". Symbols become plain objects, and the object styles they use go along. Click Add Colours to keep the colors of the drawing's document palette and its color styles as one item. The Shelf holds up to 500 items. Placing an item Drag an item onto the drawing to place a copy under the pointer. Double-click an item, or choose it and click Place, to place a copy in the middle of the view. The copies go on the active layer and are selected; one undo removes them. A color item adds its colors to the document palette and its color styles to the drawing. Arranging items Click an item to choose it. Right-click it for Place, Rename and Remove. Drag an item onto another to move it to that place. Removing an item Choose an item and click Remove. Removing cannot be undone, so TraceDraw asks first: click Remove to confirm or Cancel to keep it. Tick Do not ask again to remove items without asking; to be asked again, turn on Before an item is removed from the Shelf on the Warnings page of the global options.  Where the Shelf is kept On the desktop, the Shelf is a file in your preferences folder. In the browser, it is kept in that browser's storage, which holds only a few megabytes, so large bitmaps may not be kept.

h: Finding and replacing text Finding objects
x: Finding and replacing The Find and Replace panel (Ctrl+F) finds text in the drawing, and replaces it, or finds objects by name. Open it with Edit > Find and Replace.  Finding and replacing text Choose Text. Type what to look for in Find, and the new text in Replace with. Tick Match case to tell capitals from small letters, and Whole words only to skip the text when it is part of a longer word. Click Find Next to select the next text object that holds it, or Find All to select them all. Click Replace to replace it in the selected text, or Replace All to replace it everywhere. The panel says how many were found. Finding objects Choose Objects, type part of a name, or a kind of object such as "Rectangle", and click Find Next or Find All. The search covers the current page. To name objects, see Renaming objects and layers.

h: Adding a comment Reading and answering
x: Comments The Comments panel collects review notes on a drawing: pins, boxes and arrows on the page, each with a text and replies. Comments are saved with the drawing (in .tdraw files) and are never printed or exported. Open the panel from Window > Panels.  Adding a comment Type your name in Name. It signs your comments and replies. Left empty, the author of the drawing is used. Next to Add, click Pin, Box or Arrow. On the page, click to place a pin, or drag to draw a box around something or an arrow pointing at it. Type the comment. Each comment shows its number in an orange bubble on the page. Reading and answering The panel lists the comments, with how many are open, each with its number, author, date and time, page, text and replies. Click a card to choose the comment and go to its page; with the panel open, you can also click a bubble or a box on the page. Edit the text of the chosen comment, or type in the Reply field and press Enter or click Reply. Resolve marks a comment as dealt with; Reopen opens it again. Resolved comments are hidden unless Show resolved is ticked. Hide marks hides the bubbles, boxes and arrows on the page. Delete removes a comment and its replies. Every change is one undo step. Deleting a page deletes its comments.

h: Creating a table Typing in cells Changing rows and columns Converting text and tables
x: Tables A table is an object made of rows and columns of cells, each of which can hold text and a fill. Draw tables with the Table tool and change them with the Table menu. Creating a table Choose Table > Create New Table (or Object > Create > New Table). In the Create New Table dialog box, set the Number of Rows, the Number of Columns and the height and width (100 by 75 mm at first), and click OK. The table is placed in the middle of the page and selected. Or choose the Table tool and drag a rectangle: the table fills it, with equal rows and columns.  On the property bar of the Table tool, set the number of rows (3 at first) and columns (4 at first), the cell fill (none at first), and the border width and color. With a table selected, the fill and border change that table; otherwise they apply to the next table you draw. Typing in cells With the Table tool, click a cell and type. Text editing works as in any text: Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I and Ctrl+U format the selected characters, or the whole cell. Enter adds a line, Tab and Shift+Tab go to the next and previous cell, and the arrow keys step to the next cell at the edge of the text. A row grows when its text needs more height. Shift+click adds cells to the selection. Changing rows and columns The Table menu acts on the active cell and the selected cells: Insert: Row Above, Row Below, Column Left and Column Right. The new row or column takes the size of its neighbour. Select: Cell, Row, Column or Table. Delete: Row, Column or Table. A table keeps at least one row and one column. Distribute: Rows Evenly or Columns Evenly, keeping the size of the table. Merge Cells (Ctrl+M) makes the selected cells one cell, with their texts in order; Unmerge Cells splits it again, keeping the text and fill in the top left cell. Split into Rows and Split into Columns split the active row or column into two halves. Converting text and tables Convert Text to Table: each line of the selected text becomes a row, and tabs separate the cells. Convert Table to Text: the cells are joined by tabs and the rows by line breaks. The defaults of the tool are on the Table page of the tool options; see Tool options.

h: Making a barcode Step 1: the standard and the data Step 2: printer and sizes Step 3: the text QR codes
x: Barcodes and QR codes TraceDraw makes barcodes for products, labels and inventory, and QR codes that phones can read. Both are made of ordinary vector shapes, so they print sharp at any size. Making a barcode Choose Object > Insert > Barcode to open the Barcode Wizard. It has three steps; a Sample preview under each shows the barcode as it will be made. Use Next and Back to move between steps, and Finish on the last one.  Step 1: the standard and the data Choose one of the standards and type the data. Choosing a standard puts a sample in the field, and the wizard says what the standard accepts: Codabar: up to 30 digits and the signs - $ : / . +, between start and stop characters A to D. Code 39: capital letters, digits and - . space $ / + %. Code 128: any printable character. EAN-13, EAN-8 and UPC-A: 12, 7 or 11 digits, or one more with the check digit, optionally followed by a space and a 2- or 5-digit add-on. UPC-E: 6 digits, or the number system (0 or 1) and 6 digits. Interleaved 2 of 5: up to 40 digits. Data the standard cannot hold keeps you on this step with a message. Step 2: printer and sizes Printer: the resolution of the printer, 150 to 2400 dpi (300 at first). Bars are made a whole number of printer dots wide, so they print evenly. Units for the sizes below. Bar width reduction: printer dots taken off every bar to make up for ink spreading (1 at first). The barcode keeps its width. Magnification (scale): 100% is the standard size. Bar height (1 inch at first), with the resulting Symbol width: {w}. Wide to narrow: 2.0 to 3.0, for Codabar, Code 39 and Interleaved 2 of 5. Advanced adds Add the check character (Code 39 and Interleaved 2 of 5) and the Quiet zone, a white margin behind the bars in modules. Step 3: the text The Font, Size (12 points at first), Weight and Alignment of the readable text. Options, available where the standard uses them: Center sys/check, Place text above, Show add-on text, Add-on text at bottom, Show FACT data, Show asterisks, Show quiet zone marks and Show start/stop. Make this bar code human readable (show text): turn it off for bars without text. Finish places the barcode in the middle of the page as one group and selects it. QR codes Choose Object > Insert > QR Code. A QR code is placed in the middle of the page at once, and the Properties panel opens at its QR Code section: Choose the kind of content: URL, Email, Phone number, SMS, Contact (vCard), Text or Location. Fill in its fields, such as Address (URL), or First name, Last name, Phone number and Email address for a contact. A field applies when you leave it. Fields the kinds share are kept when you change the kind. Set the look: Pixel fill and Background fill (any fill), Pixel outline and Pixel size (2.5 mm at first). Click Validate to check that the code reads back. A green message says it does; a red one says why not, for example when the pixels are not dark enough against the background. The QR code stays editable: move, scale or turn it as any object and change its content later. To make it plain shapes, ungroup it. Content that cannot be encoded, or too much of it, changes nothing and shows in red.

Warna, isian, dan transparansi Setiap objek dapat memiliki isian di dalamnya dan garis luar di sepanjang tepinya. Halaman-halaman ini menjelaskan cara memilih warna dari palet dan panel Warna, jenis isian (warna rata, gradien, pola, tekstur, atau jaring), cara membuat objek tembus pandang, dan cara menjaga warna tetap konsisten dengan gaya warna, tinta spot, dan manajemen warna.

h: Memilih warna Mengambil sampel warna Tinta spot
x: Panel Warna Panel Warna (Shift+F11) mencampur warna dan menerapkannya ke isian atau garis luar pilihan. Alat Warna Garis Luar (Shift+F12) juga membukanya. Buka dari Jendela > Panel.  Memilih warna Pilih objek. Panel dimulai dari warna isian objek pertama. Campur warna baru di salah satu tampilan: Penampil warna: klik atau seret di dalam persegi untuk mengatur saturasi (kiri ke kanan) dan kecerahan (bawah ke atas), dan di jalur di sampingnya untuk mengatur rona; Penggeser warna: satu penggeser per komponen dari Model: RGB, CMYK (bawaan), HSB, HSL, Lab, Skala Abu-abu, atau YIQ; Palet warna: contoh warna dari sebuah palet. Tiga tombol di bagian atas menampilkan atau menyembunyikan setiap tampilan; kombinasi apa pun dapat ditampilkan. Anda juga dapat mengetik nilai #rrggbb. Klik Isian atau Garis luar di bagian bawah panel untuk menerapkan warna baru. Tambahkan ke palet menambahkannya ke palet dokumen. Warna lama dan warna baru tampil berdampingan. Bila warna baru tidak dapat dicetak tepat dengan tinta CMYK, panel menampilkan peringatan. Mengambil sampel warna Klik Pipet lalu klik di mana saja pada gambar untuk mengambil warna di sana. Lalu klik Gunakan sampel {c} untuk menjadikannya warna baru. Lihat juga Pipet. Tinta spot Di bawah tombol-tombol, Tinta spot mencantumkan tinta spot dalam gambar; lihat Warna spot.

h: Memakai palet Palet dokumen Panel Palet Menyunting palet
x: Palet warna Palet warna di sepanjang bagian bawah jendela adalah cara tercepat untuk mewarnai objek. Di bawahnya, palet dokumen mengumpulkan warna yang dipakai gambar Anda. Anda dapat membuka palet lain, membuat palet sendiri, dan menyuntingnya. Memakai palet Klik warna mengisi pilihan (bila tidak ada yang dipilih, mengatur isian objek baru) Klik kanan warna mewarnai garis luar pilihan Ctrl+klik warna mencampurkan sepersepuluh warna itu ke isian pilihan Klik dan tahan warna menampilkan gradasi lebih terang, lebih gelap, lebih kusam, dan lebih cerah untuk dipilih Seret warna ke objek mengisi objek, atau mewarnai garis luarnya bila dilepas di tepinya Klik kotak bercoret menghapus isian (klik kanan: garis luar) Panah di kedua ujung menggulir palet, dan tombol di ujung kanan menampilkan semua warna sekaligus. Arahkan penunjuk ke sebuah warna untuk melihat nama dan nilainya. Tombol menu palet di ujung kiri membuka menu palet. Palet dapat dipindahkan ke tepi jendela yang lain, atau dibuat mengambang: seret dengan pegangan bertitiknya. Palet dokumen Setiap warna yang Anda terapkan ke objek masuk ke palet dokumen, yang disimpan bersama gambar. Pipetnya menambahkan warna di bawah penunjuk, dan menunya berisi Perbarui otomatis (untuk berhenti menambahkan warna dengan sendirinya), Tambah dari pilihan, Tambah dari dokumen, Hapus warna, dan Atur ulang palet (hanya mempertahankan warna yang masih dipakai gambar). Anda juga dapat menyeret warna atau objek ke palet ini. Untuk menampilkan atau menyembunyikannya, lihat Opsi kustomisasi. Panel Palet Panel Palet mencantumkan palet yang Anda miliki, dengan jumlah warna di masing-masing. Buka dengan Jendela > Palet Warna > Pengelola Palet.  Centang palet untuk menampilkannya di bawah jendela gambar. Sunting membukanya di penyunting palet. Buka Palet membuka berkas palet (.tdpal, .gpl, .ase, atau .aco). Buat Palet dari Dokumen dan Buat Palet dari Pilihan membuat palet dari warna yang dipakai di gambar atau di pilihan. Warna palet dokumen tampil di bagian bawah; klik salah satunya untuk mengisi pilihan, klik kanan untuk mewarnai garis luar. Menyunting palet Jendela > Palet Warna > Penyunting Palet membuka penyunting palet.  Pilih Palet yang akan disunting, atau klik Baru untuk memulai yang baru. Ketik Nama. Klik warna untuk memilihnya; Tambah warna menambahkan warna saat ini dan Hapus warna menghapus warna yang dipilih. Klik Simpan palet untuk menyimpannya sebagai berkas. Klik Tutup. Palet bawaan tidak dapat disunting; buat palet baru, atau sunting salinannya.

h: Cara mengisi objek Isian seragam Isian gradien Kotak dialog Edit Isian Alat Isian Interaktif Alat Isi Area Isian jala Isian pola dan tekstur Beberapa isian pada satu objek
x: Isian Isian mewarnai bagian dalam objek tertutup. TraceDraw memiliki enam jenis isian: Tidak ada, Seragam (satu warna rata), Gradien (warna-warna yang berbaur satu sama lain), Pola, Tekstur, dan Mesh (warna yang mengalir di antara simpul-simpul kisi). Cara mengisi objek Klik warna di palet untuk memberi pilihan isian seragam. Gunakan bagian Isian di panel Properti (F11): pilih jenis isian dengan deretan gambar, lalu pengaturannya. Gunakan alat Isian Interaktif (G) untuk mengatur gradien langsung pada objek. Gunakan alat Isi Area untuk mengisi area yang dikelilingi beberapa objek. Gunakan alat Isian Jala (M) untuk isian jala. Bila tidak ada yang dipilih, isian yang Anda pilih menjadi isian objek baru. Isian seragam Isian seragam adalah satu warna, dalam model warna apa pun. Pilih dari palet, panel Warna (lihat Panel Warna), atau bagian isian di panel Properti. Isian gradien Gradien memadukan dua warna atau lebih. Pengaturannya, di bagian isian panel Properti: Jenisnya: Linier (sepanjang garis), Radial (dari pusat ke luar), Kerucut (mengelilingi pusat), Persegi (dalam persegi yang makin besar), atau Shaped (mengikuti garis luar objek, dari tepi ke dalam). Gradients: gradien siap pakai sebagai titik awal. Titik warna: warna-warna dan letaknya di sepanjang gradien, 2 sampai 64. Pilih titik untuk mengubah warna atau posisinya; Tambah titik dan Hapus titik menambah dan menghapus titik. Impor gradien mengambil warna dari berkas gradien .ggr. Sudut gradien linear, kerucut, dan persegi, bantalan tepi (seberapa banyak tiap ujung berwarna padat), dan geseran pusat gradien radial, kerucut, dan persegi. Repeat: None, Sawtooth (warna berulang lagi dari awal), atau Mirror (warna bergerak bolak-balik), dengan jumlah Cycles. Bilinear: warna bergerak dari yang pertama ke yang terakhir lalu kembali. Invert colours: warna bergerak dalam urutan terbalik. Sebuah jalur di bawah jenis menampilkan seluruh urutan warna seperti yang akan digambar. Kotak dialog Edit Isian F11 membuka kotak dialog Edit Fill pada isian pilihan. Untuk gradien, kotak ini menampilkan pratinjau, Fill picker, jenis, pengulangan, dan pita warna: klik node untuk memilihnya, seret untuk memindahkannya, klik ganda untuk menambah atau menghapus node. Di bawah pita: warna, transparansi, posisi, dan Midpoint node, serta Reverse. Transform berisi rotasi, pusat, dan bantalan tepi. OK menerapkan yang Anda ubah, dengan Overprint fill. Selama kotak dialog terbuka, seleksi menampilkan isian saat Anda mengubahnya; Batal atau Esc mengembalikan isian lama.  Alat Isian Interaktif Alat Isian Interaktif (G) menyunting isian langsung pada objek. Pilih alat lalu seret melintasi objek: Anda mendapat gradien linear dari tempat Anda menekan hingga tempat Anda melepas. Tahan Ctrl untuk membatasi sudut ke kelipatan 15 derajat. Satu klik memberi isian bawaan. Seret simpul pada objek untuk mengubah gradien: dua simpul persegi pada gradien linear mengubah arah dan panjangnya; simpul gradien radial, kerucut, atau persegi memindahkan pusatnya. Seret warna palet ke sebuah simpul untuk mewarnainya ulang, atau ke garis di antara simpul untuk menambah warna di sana. Bilah properti berisi jenis isian dan pengaturannya: warna isian seragam; untuk gradien, jenisnya, warna awal dan akhir, sudut, dan bantalan tepi. Alat Isi Area Alat Isi Area mengisi area tertutup apa pun, bahkan yang terbentuk dari beberapa objek yang saling tumpang tindih, dengan membuat objek baru dari area itu. Objek di sekitarnya tetap seperti semula. Pilih alat Isi Area. Pilih isian dan garis luar di bilah properti: Gunakan bawaan (isian dan garis luar objek baru; sebuah warna bila bawaannya tanpa isian, agar area terlihat), Tentukan (warnanya, dan untuk garis luar juga lebarnya, di sampingnya), atau Tidak ada. Klik di dalam area. Objek baru diletakkan di atas lapisan aktif dan dipilih. Klik pada garis luar, atau di area yang tidak dikelilingi apa pun, tidak menghasilkan apa-apa. Isian jala Isian jala adalah kisi simpul di atas objek, setiap simpul dengan warna dan transparansinya sendiri; warna mengalir halus di antara simpul. Cocok untuk bayangan yang realistis. Pilih alat Isian Jala (M) lalu atur baris dan kolom di bilah properti (awalnya 2 kali 2, hingga 50). Klik sebuah objek. Objek mendapat jala dengan warna isiannya. Klik simpul untuk memilihnya, lalu klik warna di palet untuk mewarnainya. Seret simpul untuk membelokkan aliran warna. Klik ganda di dalam jala untuk menambah baris atau kolom melalui simpul terdekat; pilih simpul lalu tekan Delete untuk menghapus baris dan kolomnya. Bilah properti juga berisi Warna halus, yang memadukan warna dengan lebih lembut, transparansi simpul yang dipilih, dan Hapus jala, yang menghapus isian jala. Mengubah baris dan kolom jala tetap mempertahankan warnanya. Isian pola dan tekstur Isian Pola mengulang sebuah ubin: dua warna, pola vektor, atau bitmap. Lihat Isian pola. Isian Tekstur adalah tekstur hasil olahan yang tampak alami: Awan, Marmer, Noise, atau Kayu, dengan warna dan skalanya. Beberapa isian pada satu objek Di bagian isian panel Properti, Tambah isian melukis isian lain di atas isian objek itu sendiri, dimulai sebagai salinan untuk diubah. Isian berikutnya tampil sebagai "Isian 2", "Isian 3", dan seterusnya, masing- masing dengan penyuntingnya sendiri dan tombol untuk menghapusnya. Bagian garis luar dapat menambahkan garis luar lain dengan cara yang sama. Isian juga dapat dilukis pada garis luar; lihat Mengatur garis luar.

h: Membuat pola dari objek Anda Pengaturan pola Pola dalam berkas ekspor
x: Isian pola Isian pola mengulang sebuah ubin di seluruh bagian dalam objek. Ubin dapat berupa dua warna, sekumpulan objek vektor (pola vektor penuh warna), atau bitmap. Ubin ditambatkan ke halaman, jadi tidak bergeser saat Anda memindahkan objek. Membuat pola dari objek Anda Gambar objek-objek yang membentuk satu ubin lalu pilih objek-objek itu. Pilih Objek > Buat > Isian Pola. Di kotak dialog Buat pola, pilih Jenis: Vektor mempertahankan objek sebagai vektor, tetap tajam pada ukuran berapa pun; Bitmap membuat gambar dari objek-objek itu. Klik OK.  Pola menjadi isian objek baru. Untuk memberikannya ke objek yang sudah Anda gambar, pilih Pola di bagian isian panel Properti. Pengaturan pola Di bagian isian panel Properti, pilih Pola, lalu jenis pola dan pengaturannya. Untuk pola vektor, panel menampilkan berapa banyak objek yang ada di dalam ubin, serta lebar dan tingginya: mengubahnya akan ikut menskalakan isi ubin. Pola dalam berkas ekspor Berkas SVG mempertahankan pola vektor sebagai vektor. Berkas PDF dan EPS menerimanya sebagai gambar pada resolusi ekspor, dipotong mengikuti objek.

t: Menyalin warna dan atribut dengan pipet
h: Pipet Warna Pipet Atribut
x: Menyalin warna dan atribut dengan pipet Alat pipet mengambil warna, atau seluruh kumpulan atribut, dari satu objek dan memberikannya ke objek lain. Keduanya bekerja dalam dua langkah, yang tampil di bilah properti: pilih (ambil sampel) dan terapkan (lukis dengannya). Setelah mengambil sampel, alat beralih ke terapkan; klik tombol pilih untuk mengambil sampel lagi. Esc membuang sampel dan kembali ke alat Pilih. Penunjuk berupa pipet saat alat mengambil sampel dan ember cat saat menerapkan. Gambar memberikan warnanya meski di dalam grup atau bingkai. Pipet Warna Pilih alat Pipet Warna. Klik objek untuk mengambil warnanya: warna isian dari isian seragam, warna pertama dari gradien, atau warna garis luar. Pada bitmap, alat ini mengambil warna piksel di bawah penunjuk, dirata-ratakan sesuai ukuran sampel yang diatur di bilah properti (1 kali 1, 2 kali 2, atau 5 kali 5 piksel). Shift+klik mengambil warna garis luar lebih dahulu. Klik objek untuk mengisinya dengan warna itu; Shift+klik untuk mewarnai garis luarnya (objek tanpa garis luar mendapat garis tipis). Klik di dalam bentuk tertutup yang kosong akan mengisinya. Bilah properti menampilkan warna sampel. Pipet Atribut Alat Pipet Atribut menyalin beberapa properti sekaligus dari satu objek ke objek lain. Pilih alat Pipet Atribut. Di bilah properti, pilih apa yang disalin: Properti: garis luar, isian, dan teks (fon, ukuran, dan gaya; teksnya sendiri tetap). Semua awalnya aktif. Transformasi: ukuran, rotasi, dan posisi. Awalnya nonaktif. Efek: transparansi, bayangan jatuh, dan efek langsung. Awalnya nonaktif. Klik objek sumber. Klik setiap objek tujuan. Shift+klik justru mengambil sampel dari objek lain. Setiap klik adalah satu langkah urungkan.

h: Membuat gaya warna Memakai dan menyunting gaya Harmoni
x: Gaya warna Gaya warna adalah warna bernama yang dipakai objek dalam gambar. Ubah gayanya dan setiap objek yang diisi dengannya ikut berubah, sehingga warna desain tetap konsisten dan skema warna lain dapat dicoba dengan cepat. Gaya dicantumkan di panel Gaya Warna; buka dari Jendela > Panel.  Membuat gaya warna Baru dari pilihan menambahkan gaya untuk setiap warna isian objek terpilih yang belum menjadi gaya. Gaya warna baru menambahkan gaya dari warna saat ini di panel Warna. Memakai dan menyunting gaya Setiap gaya menampilkan warnanya, namanya, dan tiga tombol: klik warnanya untuk mengubahnya: objek yang diisi dengan warna itu ikut berubah; klik namanya untuk mengganti nama; Isian mengisi pilihan dengan gaya itu, Garis luar mewarnai garis luarnya; x menghapus gaya (objek tetap mempertahankan warnanya). Harmoni Penyunting harmoni membuat sekumpulan gaya yang serasi, dari sebuah Warna dasar: Pilih Warna dasar. Klik sebuah harmoni: Analog, Komplementer, Komplementer terpisah, Triadik, Tetradik, atau Monokromatik. Warna-warna harmoni ditambahkan sebagai gaya, dinamai sesuai harmoninya.

h: Menerapkan transparansi Pengaturan
x: Transparansi Transparansi membuat apa yang ada di bawah objek terlihat menembusnya. Transparansi dapat sama di seluruh objek, berubah di sepanjang objek seperti gradien, atau mengikuti pola atau tekstur. Menerapkan transparansi Dengan alat Transparansi: klik objek, lalu pilih jenis transparansi di bilah properti, atau seret melintasi objek untuk transparansi gradien dari buram (tempat Anda menekan) hingga transparan (tempat Anda melepas). Simpul gradien lalu tampil pada objek, seperti pada alat Isian Interaktif: seret awal, akhir, atau simpul miring yang bulat; seret batang di antara dua simpul (titik tengah) untuk memindahkan tempat campuran mencapai setengah; klik ganda garis untuk menambah simpul, dan simpul untuk menghapusnya. Di bagian Transparansi pada panel Properti. Pengaturan Jenisnya: Tanpa transparansi, Seragam (bawaan), Gradien (linear, radial, kerucut, persegi, atau berbentuk, seperti isian gradien), Pola, atau Tekstur. Jumlahnya: 0 sampai 100% (awalnya 50%). Untuk gradien, titik warnanya berupa gradasi abu-abu: putih berarti buram, hitam berarti sepenuhnya transparan. Mode gabung: cara warna bercampur dengan apa yang ada di bawahnya. Normal (bawaan) hanya memperlihatkan yang di bawah; mode lain, seperti Tambah, Kurangi, Selisih, Kalikan, Bagi, Bila lebih terang, Bila lebih gelap, Rona, Saturasi, Warna, dan Balikkan, menggabungkan warna dengan cara lain. Apakah berlaku untuk Isian, Garis luar, atau Semua. Bekukan: mempertahankan apa yang terlihat menembus seperti saat ini, meskipun objek di bawahnya berpindah. Untuk menyalin transparansi objek lain, gunakan Objek > Salin Efek > Transparansi Dari. Untuk area tembus pandang yang ditentukan oleh kecerahan objek, lihat Masker opasitas.

h: Menambahkan tinta spot Memakai tinta spot Buku warna Warna spot dalam cetakan dan ekspor
x: Warna spot Warna spot adalah tinta bernama yang dicetak di pelatnya sendiri, misalnya warna metalik atau warna merek, alih-alih dicampur dari cyan, magenta, kuning, dan hitam. Setiap gambar menyimpan daftar tinta spotnya. Setiap tinta memiliki pengganti yang terbuat dari warna proses, dipakai untuk menampilkannya di layar dan di mana pun tinta itu tidak dapat dipakai. Menambahkan tinta spot Buka panel Warna dan campur warna yang akan menjadi tampilan tinta itu. Di bawah Tinta spot, ketik Nama tinta. Klik Tinta spot baru. Nama bersifat unik di dalam satu gambar. Memakai tinta spot Daftar Tinta spot menampilkan setiap tinta dengan contoh warna, namanya, serta tombol Isian dan Garis luar, yang menerapkannya ke pilihan pada Tint yang Anda atur (0 sampai 100%, awalnya 100%). Tanda silang di ujung baris menghapus tinta dari daftar; objek yang memakainya tetap mempertahankan warna penggantinya. Buku warna Berkas palet dapat berupa buku tinta spot (misalnya palet .ase dengan entri spot). Entri spotnya terbuka sebagai warna spot, dinamai seperti di buku; menerapkan salah satunya menambahkan tinta ke gambar. TraceDraw tidak menyertakan buku warna berlisensi, tetapi buku yang Anda miliki dapat dibuka seperti palet lainnya. Warna spot dalam cetakan dan ekspor Dalam berkas PDF, setiap tinta menjadi warna separasi yang dinamai sesuai tinta itu, sehingga percetakan menerima tintanya. Saat Anda mencetak separasi, setiap tinta mendapat pelatnya sendiri setelah pelat cyan, magenta, kuning, dan hitam. Lihat Mencetak. Di layar dan dalam berkas bitmap, SVG, dan .cdr, warna spot tampil sebagai penggantinya pada tingkat rona yang diatur.

h: Profil gambar Bawaan untuk gambar baru Pratinjau warna cetak
x: Manajemen warna Layar menampilkan warna dengan cahaya merah, hijau, dan biru; printer mencampur tinta cyan, magenta, kuning, dan hitam. Manajemen warna memakai profil warna untuk menggambarkan setiap perangkat, sehingga warna tetap terlihat sama dari layar hingga halaman cetak. Pengaturannya ada di Alat > Manajemen Warna, kotak dialog Pengaturan manajemen warna. Tidak ada yang berubah sampai Anda mengklik OK.  Profil gambar Tab Dokumen mengatur profil gambar yang aktif. Profil saat ini menampilkan profil RGB, CMYK, dan skala abu-abu yang dipakai gambar saat ini. Pilih cara profil baru diterapkan: Tetapkan baru (pertahankan nilai warna): nilai warna tetap dan tampilannya berubah mengikuti profil baru; Konversi (pertahankan tampilan warna): warna CMYK dikonversi agar terlihat sama di profil baru. Pilih profil Profil RGB, Profil CMYK, dan Skala abu-abu. Setiap daftar berisi profil bawaan, lalu setiap profil yang ditemukan di komputer Anda. Muat profil warna menambahkan berkas profil (.icc, .icm). Mode warna utama: CMYK atau RGB. Tujuan rendering: cara warna yang tidak dapat ditampilkan dibawa masuk: Kolorimetrik relatif (bawaan), Perseptual, Saturasi, atau Kolorimetrik absolut. Profil CMYK ikut tersimpan bersama gambar, juga ke dalam berkas .cdr sejak versi 16. Bawaan untuk gambar baru Tab Bawaan mengatur apa yang dipakai gambar baru, dan cara warna dikonversi. Preset: pengaturan siap pakai untuk Amerika Utara, Eropa, Jepang, atau pekerjaan web dan layar. Simpan preset menyimpan pengaturan Anda sendiri dengan Nama preset; Hapus preset menghapusnya. Profil RGB, Profil CMYK, dan Profil skala abu-abu bawaan, Mode warna utama, serta Tujuan rendering. Konversi warna: Mesin warna: Mesin ICC TraceDraw, yang memakai profil, atau Rumus bawaan; Pertahankan hitam murni: warna yang hanya berupa tinta hitam tetap hanya tinta hitam saat dikonversi; Petakan abu-abu ke hitam CMYK (awalnya aktif): abu-abu yang dikonversi ke CMYK hanya memakai tinta hitam; Kompensasi titik hitam (awalnya aktif): menjaga gradasi tergelap tetap terpisah. Kebijakan membuka: apa yang terjadi pada profil berkas yang Anda buka, untuk RGB, CMYK, dan skala abu-abu: Gunakan profil warna tersemat, Tetapkan profil warna bawaan, atau Konversi ke profil warna bawaan. Peringatkan bila profil warna berbeda dan Peringatkan bila profil warna tidak ada menampilkan pesan di bilah status bila sebuah berkas memiliki profil lain atau tidak memiliki profil. Kebijakan impor dan tempel: Konversi ke profil warna dokumen atau Tetapkan profil warna dokumen, untuk apa yang Anda impor atau tempel. Definisi warna spot: apakah warna spot ditentukan oleh Nilai Lab, Nilai CMYK, atau Nilai RGB. Pratinjau warna cetak Tampilan > Warna Pruf, atau tombol uji cetak di ujung kanan bilah status, menampilkan gambar seperti saat dicetak: warna yang tidak dapat dicetak tinta CMYK terlihat lebih kusam. Panel Warna juga memperingatkan tentang warna semacam itu. Tanpa profil yang dimuat, TraceDraw mengonversi warna dengan modelnya sendiri untuk tinta proses di atas kertas berlapis.

Efek khusus Efek mengubah tampilan objek tanpa mengubah objeknya: paduan mengisi ruang antara dua objek, kontur menggambar cincin di sekeliling objek, amplop membengkokkannya, ekstrusi membuatnya tampak padat, bayangan memisahkannya dari halaman. Sebagian besar efek bersifat hidup: objek mempertahankan bentuknya sendiri dan efek digambar darinya, sehingga Anda dapat mengubah atau menghapus efek kapan saja. Efek ada di menu Efek, di menu lipat Efek pada kotak alat, dan di panelnya sendiri. Efek bitmap mengubah piksel gambar, atau piksel objek yang digambar sebagai gambar.

h: Managing effects Other effect commands
x: The Effects panel An object can carry several live effects at once, applied one after the other. The Effects panel lists the effects of the selected object in the order they apply, from the top down. Open it with Window > Panels > Effects.  Managing effects Each row of the list has: a check box that turns the effect on or off. An effect turned off keeps its place and settings, but is not drawn, exported or printed; the effect's name, dimmed while it is off; up and down arrows that move the effect earlier or later, which changes the result (for example a contour of an envelope, or an envelope of a contour); a cross that removes the effect. Every change is one undo step. Each effect is still edited with its own tool or panel. Other effect commands Effects > Flatten Effects turns the effects of the selected objects into plain objects. Effect Picker shows a list of effects to apply to the selection. Object > Clear Effect removes the effect of the selection. Object > Copy Effect copies an effect from another object, and Clone Effect makes a clone that follows it; see Copying and cloning effects.

h: To blend two objects Blend settings Blending along a path Removing or splitting a blend
x: Blends A blend draws a series of intermediate steps between two objects, changing shape, size and color from one to the other. Use it for smooth shading, repeated patterns or a shape that turns into another. To blend two objects With the tool: Choose the Blend tool from the Effects flyout. Drag from the start object to the end object. With the panel: Select two objects. Open the Blend panel with Effects > Blend (Ctrl+F8). Set the options and click Apply.  Both objects stay objects of the drawing: move, resize or recolor either one and the steps follow. Deleting the end object removes the blend. Blend settings With a blend selected, every change on the property bar or in the panel applies at once. Blend steps: the number of steps (5 at first, up to 999). Spacing, for a blend on a path: the distance between steps; the number of steps follows from the length of the path. Rotation: turns the steps progressively; Loop turns them about the middle between the two objects instead. Acceleration: the object slider makes the steps crowd towards one end; the color slider does the same for the colors. Apply to sizing makes the object acceleration change the sizes too, and Link acceleration keeps the two sliders together. Reset puts both back to even. Color Blend: Direct (straight from one color to the other), Clockwise or Counterclockwise (around the color wheel). The tool's property bar has the steps, rotation and the two accelerations. Blending along a path Select the blend. Click New path in the Blend panel and click a curve. The steps follow the curve. Rotate all objects turns each step along the curve, and Blend along full path places the first and last steps at the ends of the curve. Removing or splitting a blend Clear blend removes the steps and leaves both objects. Break apart turns the steps into objects of their own, grouped. Object > Break Blend Group Apart (Ctrl+K, also on the right-click menu) does the same.

h: To add a contour Contour settings
x: Contours A contour draws evenly spaced copies of an object's outline inside it, outside it, or to its center, like the lines of a map. It is a live effect: change the object and the contour follows. To add a contour With the tool: Choose the Contour tool from the Effects flyout. Drag from an object: away from its middle for an outside contour, towards it for an inside one. The further you drag, the larger the spacing. With the panel: Select an object. Open the Contour panel with Effects > Contour (Ctrl+F9). Set the options and click Apply.  Groups and bitmaps cannot take a contour. Contour settings The property bar and the panel show the settings of the selected contour and change it at once. To center, Inside or Outside (at first). Steps: 3 at first, up to 999. To center makes as many as fit. Offset: the distance between steps (2 mm at first). Corners: mitered (sharp, at first), round or beveled. Color direction: direct, clockwise or counterclockwise around the color wheel, from the object's colors to the last step's. The fill and outline colors of the last step (white and black at first). An object without a fill gives unfilled steps. Object acceleration and color acceleration (-100 to 100%) crowd the steps or the colors towards the object or towards the last step. Outside steps are drawn behind the object, inside steps in front of it. Clear contour removes the contour; Break apart turns the steps into objects, grouped beside the object. Object > Break Contour Group Apart (Ctrl+K, also on the right-click menu) does the same.

h: To distort an object Distortion settings
x: Distortion The Distort tool bends an object's outline in three ways: push and pull (spikes or petals), zipper (zigzag teeth) and twister (a swirl). It is a live effect: you can change, move or remove the distortion at any time, and the object keeps its own outline. To distort an object Choose the Distort tool from the Effects flyout. Choose the kind on the property bar. Drag on the object. The distortion is centered where you start. Push and pull: drag right to push the nodes out (spiky shapes with hollow sides), left to pull them in (rounded petals). Zipper: the further you drag, the taller the teeth. Twister: drag around the starting point; full turns count. The center of a selected distortion shows as a diamond: drag it to move the center. Dragging again replaces the distortion; an object has at most one. Groups and bitmaps are not distorted. Distortion settings The property bar shows and changes the selected distortion: the kind: Push and pull, Zipper or Twister (choosing another kind changes a selected distortion); for push and pull, the amplitude (-200 to 200, 20 at first); for zipper, the amplitude (0 to 100 mm, 2 mm at first) and the frequency (teeth per segment, 6 at first), with Random (uneven teeth), Smooth (rounded teeth) and Local (teeth shrink away from the center); for twister, clockwise or counterclockwise, the number of whole rotations and the extra degrees. Object > Clear Effect removes the distortion.

h: To add an envelope Editing the frame Envelope settings
x: Envelopes An envelope is a frame of nodes around an object; the object is bent to fill the frame, and follows when you move its nodes. Use it to arch text, bulge a shape or fit artwork into a flag or a circle. The object keeps its own shape, so the envelope can be changed or removed at any time. To add an envelope With the tool: Choose the Envelope tool from the Effects flyout. Click an object. It gets a frame of eight nodes: the corners and the middle of each side. Drag the nodes to reshape the frame. With the panel (Effects > Envelope, Ctrl+F7): Select an object. Click Add new, or click one of the 24 preset shapes (arch, circle, flag, heart, cloud, speech bubble and more) to use it as the envelope.  Editing the frame The editing mode, chosen on the property bar or in the panel, decides what happens to the sides when you drag a node: Straight line: the sides stay straight; Single arc: the sides become one smooth arc; Double arc: the sides become S curves; Unconstrained (at first): the node carries its handles; click a node to see its two handles and drag them to bend each side on its own. Double-click the frame to add a node, a node (other than a corner) to delete it. In the unconstrained mode the property bar also has Add node and Delete node. The Shape tool edits the frame the same way. Envelope settings Presets on the property bar: arch, bulge, squeeze, flag, perspective and circle. Mapping, how the object fills the frame: Putty (at first), Original (spread evenly along the frame), Horizontal or Vertical (only across or only up). Keep lines: straight segments of the object stay straight. Add new envelope puts a fresh frame around the object as it now looks, over the envelope it has. Copy envelope properties: click another object to copy its envelope (as Object > Copy Effect > Envelope From). Clear envelope removes the last envelope.

h: Place the photo and the design Follow the chest with an envelope Let the cloth show through: Multiply Keep the print on the shirt: a clip frame Tips
x: Making a T-shirt mockup A mockup shows a design on a photo of the real thing, here a T-shirt, so you can judge it before it is printed. Four tools from the rest of this Help do the work: an envelope bends the design over the chest, a transparency merge mode lets the cloth's folds and shading show through the print, and a clip frame keeps the print on the shirt.  Place the photo and the design Choose File > Import and import a photo of a plain shirt, front view, in good light. Draw or import your design, place it over the chest and size it there. If the design is made of several objects, select them all and choose Object > Group, so the next steps treat it as one. Follow the chest with an envelope Cloth is not flat. A slight curve makes the print look as if it lies on the shirt. Select the design and choose the Envelope tool (or open Effects > Envelope). Use Single arc and drag the middle nodes a little: the bottom one down, the top one up and the side ones out. Keep it subtle. Each object of a group is bent from the box of the whole group and keeps its own colours. See Envelopes.  Let the cloth show through: Multiply A print takes on the shading of the cloth under it. The Multiply merge mode does the same: each color is multiplied by what is beneath, so the folds and shadows of the photo darken the design where they darken the shirt. Select the design and choose the Transparency tool, or open the transparency settings in the Properties panel. Choose Uniform and set the amount low (0 to 10 %). Set Merge mode to Multiply. See Transparency.  Keep the print on the shirt: a clip frame A large print, or one placed near a sleeve, can reach past the shirt's edges.  Draw the outline of the shirt over the photo with the Bezier or Pen tool, following its edges (it does not need to be exact where the print does not reach). Give it no fill and no outline. Select the design, choose Object > Clip to Frame > Place Inside Frame and click the outline. The print is cut to the shirt and keeps its Multiply merge mode: it still mixes with the photo beneath the frame. See Placing objects inside a frame.  Tips A white or light shirt shows Multiply best. On a dark shirt, try If Lighter for a light print, or keep Normal with a little transparency. To try another design, use Edit Contents, or Extract Contents, replace the design and place the new one inside again. Group the photo, the frame and the design to move the whole mockup.

h: To extrude an object Extrusion settings
x: Extrusions An extrusion turns a flat object into a solid-looking body, with sides that run from its outline to a copy of it, lit and shaded. It is a live effect: change the object and the body follows. To extrude an object With the tool: Choose the Extrude tool from the Effects flyout. Drag from an object. For a parallel extrusion the body runs along the drag; for the others the end of the drag is the vanishing point. Drag the handle (a square with a cross) to move the vanishing point. With the panel (Effects > Extrude, Ctrl+F10): select an object, set the options and click Apply.  Groups and bitmaps cannot be extruded. Extrusion settings The panel has five pages, chosen with the buttons at its top; the property bar has the main settings and a 3D menu with the rest. Camera: the type of extrusion: small back (at first), big back, small front, big front, back parallel or front parallel. Back types grow behind the object, front types in front of it. The depth (1 to 99, 20 at first), the vanishing point (X and Y, counted from the page origin or the object's center), and whether it is locked to the object (moves with it) or to the page. For parallel types, X and Y are the offset. Rotation: turns the body in space about X, Y and Z (-360 to 360 degrees); Reset puts it back. Lighting: the angle (135 degrees at first), intensity (50 at first) and elevation of the light, and two more lights you can turn on. Color: Object fill (the object's color, at first), Solid (one color) or Shade (a gradient from one color to another on each side). Bevel: a beveled edge on the front face, with its width. Clear extrude removes the extrusion; Break apart turns the faces into objects, grouped beside the object. Object > Break Extrude Group Apart (Ctrl+K, also on the right-click menu) does the same.

h: To add a block shadow Settings
x: Block shadows A block shadow is a solid shadow that runs straight out from an object, as if the object were a thick block. It is drawn below the object as one filled shape, which suits signs and cut vinyl. To add a block shadow Choose the Block Shadow tool from the Effects flyout. Drag from an object in the direction the shadow should go. Settings On the property bar: Depth: how far the shadow reaches. Direction: its angle, 0 being to the right, counterclockwise. Color: 60% black at first. Gap: a clear band between the object and the shadow (0 at first). Clear block shadow removes the effect. With a shadowed object selected, the fields change its shadow; otherwise they set the next one.

h: To add a drop shadow Settings
x: Drop shadows A drop shadow is a soft shadow beneath an object, as if it floated above the page. It is a copy of the object's silhouette in the shadow color, offset and blurred. To add a drop shadow Choose the Drop Shadow tool from the Effects flyout. Drag from an object to where the shadow should fall. Settings On the property bar: the offset of the shadow (2 mm right and 2 mm down at first); its opacity (50% at first); its feathering, how soft its edge is (15% at first); its color (black at first). Object > Clear Effect removes the shadow. To copy the shadow of another object, use Object > Copy Effect > Drop Shadow From.

h: Untuk memberi bevel pada objek
x: Bevel Bevel membuat tepi objek terlihat timbul atau terukir, dengan menerangi satu sisi tepi dan membayangi sisi lainnya. Ini adalah efek langsung, diatur di panel Bevel; buka dengan Efek > Bevel.  Untuk memberi bevel pada objek Pilih objek yang berisi isian. Di panel Bevel, pilih gayanya: Tepi lembut: tepi melandai ke dalam objek, terang di satu sisi dan berbayang di sisi lain; Timbul: objek tampak menonjol keluar dari halaman. Atur Jarak (seberapa jauh bevel masuk ke dalam objek), Sudut cahaya, Intensitas cahaya, Warna bayangan, dan Warna cahaya. Klik Terapkan. Untuk menyalin bevel dari objek lain, gunakan Objek > Salin Efek > Bevel dari. Objek > Bersihkan Efek menghapusnya. Panel ekstrusi juga memiliki bevel untuk sisi depan; lihat Ekstrusi.

h: To make a lens Kinds of lens Options
x: Lenses A lens changes how the objects beneath it look, without changing them: it can brighten, tint, magnify, invert or apply bitmap effects to everything it covers. Move the lens and the view through it changes. Lenses are set in the Lens panel (Effects > Lens, Alt+F3).  To make a lens Draw a closed object over the objects to change, and select it. In the Lens panel, choose the kind of lens and its settings. Click Apply. Kinds of lens Brighten brightens (or darkens) what lies beneath rate, -100 to 100 (50) Color add adds a color, as light color and rate Color limit lets only a color through color and rate Custom color map maps dark to light onto a range of colors from and to colors, direction Fish eye bulges what lies beneath rate, -1000 to 1000 (100) Heat map shows brightness as warm and cold colors palette rotation Invert inverts the colors  Magnify enlarges what lies beneath amount, 1 to 100 (2) Tinted grayscale shows it in shades of one color color Transparency makes the lens see-through, tinted rate and color Wireframe shows the objects as outlines outline and fill colors Bitmap effects runs bitmap effects over what lies beneath Add effect, in order Options Frozen: keeps what the lens shows now, even when the objects beneath change. Viewpoint: shows another place through the lens. Remove face: shows the lens only over other objects, not over the empty page. To add a bitmap effect as a lens from the effect picker, choose Effects > Effect Picker and apply it as a lens.

h: Adding perspective to an object Drawing in perspective
x: Perspective Perspective makes an object look as if it lay on a plane that recedes into the distance. You can add perspective to an object you have drawn, or draw straight onto a perspective grid. Adding perspective to an object Select an object. Choose Object > Add Perspective. Drag the four corner nodes with the Shape tool to tilt it. To copy the perspective of another object, use Object > Copy Effect > Perspective From. Drawing in perspective View > Draw in Perspective shows a perspective grid over the page. While it is on, every object a drawing tool makes (rectangles, ellipses, polygons, curves, brush strokes, text frames) is laid onto the active plane of the grid. Objects you paste, duplicate or move with the Pick tool stay as they are. The bar at the top left of the drawing window has: Finish: leaves the mode; the objects keep their perspective; 1-Point, 2-Point and 3-Point: the kind of grid; the planes: Ground, Left, Right (and Top for a 1-point grid). The active plane is drawn strongly; Grid: shows the grid lines; Depth (5 to 98%): how far the grid reaches towards the vanishing points; Put on plane: lays the selected objects onto the active plane. Drag the vanishing points (circles) and the near corners (squares) to change the grid. An object laid on a plane gets an ordinary perspective effect, whose four corners you can still edit with the Shape tool.

h: Copying an effect Cloning an effect
x: Copying and cloning effects Instead of setting up an effect again, you can copy it from an object that already has it. Copying an effect Select the objects that should get the effect. Choose Object > Copy Effect and the kind of effect: Drop Shadow From, Transparency From, Envelope From, Perspective From, Distortion From, Extrude From, Contour From, Blend From, Lens From, Bevel From or Block Shadow From. Click the object to copy from. A right-click cancels. The effect is fitted to each object: an envelope or perspective is stretched to its size, a distortion keeps its center at the same place within it. When the object you click has no such effect, nothing changes and the status bar says so. The copy is one undo step. Cloning an effect Object > Clone Effect copies the shadow (Shadow From) or the transparency (Transparency From) of another object, and keeps following it: change the source and the clones change too, until you edit a clone's own effect. Edit > Clone makes a clone of a whole object, and Copy Properties From copies the fill, outline or text properties of another object.

h: Vector Mosaic Picture Mosaic
x: Vector and picture mosaics A mosaic rebuilds the selected objects, or a picture, out of many small tiles. A vector mosaic uses colored shapes; a picture mosaic uses photos from a folder of your own. Vector Mosaic Open the Vector Mosaic panel with Effects > Vector Mosaic.  Select the objects or bitmaps to turn into a mosaic. Set the options: Density: tiles per inch (10 at first); Scale: the size of each tile within its cell (1 at first); Screen angle: how the rows are turned (30 degrees at first). Keep original: off deletes the selection once the mosaic is made. Limit colors: reduce the tiles to at most that many colors (16 at first). Method: Uniform (every tile full size, transparency flattened on white), Size modulation 1 (the tile size follows the opacity, at first) or Size modulation 2 (darker areas give bigger tiles). Merge adjacent: combine up to that many neighbouring tiles of one color; Weld adjacent overlap: one curve per color instead of one object per tile. Shape: circle (at first), square or custom. For a custom tile, select a closed curve and click Select. Click Apply. The mosaic is one group placed on top of the selection, and is selected. Picture Mosaic Open the Picture Mosaic panel with Effects > Picture Mosaic.  Select the objects or bitmaps to rebuild. Under Library, click Browse and choose a folder of pictures (PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF, WebP or TIFF; up to 1000). The panel shows how many it holds. Set the options: Keep original (on at first). Columns: tiles across (30 at first); the rows follow from the shape of the selection. Blending: how much of the selection shows over the tiles (20% at first). Allow duplicates (on), with the tile spacing: the fewest tiles between two uses of one picture. Composition: single, stack or array; Edges: stretch the last row or remove it; Output priority and the resolution: how large the mosaic is in pixels. The panel shows the resulting size. Click Apply. Note: Picture libraries need the desktop version; the browser version cannot read folders.

h: Untuk menerapkan efek bitmap Kelompok efek Dialog khusus Menyunting efek sebuah objek Pemilih Efek Efek yang menyebar melewati tepi
x: Efek bitmap Efek bitmap mengubah piksel: mengaburkan, mempertajam, menyesuaikan warna, menambahkan tekstur dan goresan artistik. Efek ini bekerja pada bitmap dan juga pada objek vektor, yang kemudian digambar sebagai gambar hasil efek sambil tetap mempertahankan bentuk, isian, dan garis luarnya sendiri. Efek disimpan terpisah dari piksel asli: Anda dapat menyunting, menyembunyikan, mengubah urutan, atau menghapus efek mana pun nanti, dan menghapus efek terakhir mengembalikan gambar aslinya. Untuk menerapkan efek bitmap Pilih satu objek atau lebih. Pilih kelompok di menu Efek lalu sebuah efek. Efek tanpa pengaturan langsung diterapkan. Efek lainnya membuka kotak dialog dengan pratinjau sebelum dan sesudah dari objek pertama yang dipilih: atur nilainya lalu klik OK. Atur ulang mengembalikan setiap pengaturan ke bawaannya.  Perubahan pada seluruh pilihan adalah satu langkah urungkan. Bila bitmap dipilih, Ctrl+B membuka Kecerahan/Kontras/Intensitas, Ctrl+Shift+B Keseimbangan Warna, dan Ctrl+Shift+U Rona/Saturasi/Kecerahan. Kelompok efek Efek 3D Silinder, Timbul, Gulungan Halaman, Cubit/Tekan, Bola Sesuaikan Penyesuaian Otomatis, Penyesuaian Gambar, Peningkatan Kontras, Penyamaan Lokal, Keseimbangan Warna Target, Kurva Nada, Kecerahan/Kontras/Intensitas, Keseimbangan Warna, Gamma, Rona/Saturasi/Kecerahan, Warna Selektif, Ganti Warna, Hilangkan Saturasi, Pencampur Saluran Sapuan Seni Arang, Krayon Conté, Krayon, Kubisme, Impresionis, Pisau Palet, Pastel, Pena & Tinta, Pointilis, Papan Gores, Sketsa, Cat Air, Spidol, Butiran Kertas Buram Penghalusan Terarah, Kabur Gaussian, Haluskan Tepi Bergerigi, Lolos Rendah, Kabur Gerak, Kabur Radial, Kabur Cerdas, Haluskan, Lembutkan, Zoom Kamera Warnai, Difus, Filter Foto, Nada Sepia, Foto Antik Transformasi Warna Bidang Bit, Halftone, Psikedelik, Solarisasi Kontur Deteksi Tepi, Cari Tepi, Telusuri Kontur Koreksi Debu dan Goresan Kreatif Kristalisasi, Kain, Bingkai, Ubin Kaca, Mozaik, Sebar, Kaca Berwarna, Kaca Patri, Vinyet, Pusaran Kustom Peta Tonjolan Distorsi Blok, Pindahkan, Lengkung Jaring, Geser, Pikselasi, Riak, Putaran, Ubin, Cat Basah, Pusaran Air, Angin Derau Tambah Derau, Maksimum, Median, Minimum, Hapus Moiré, Hapus Derau Pertajam Penajaman Adaptif, Penajaman Terarah, Lolos Tinggi, Pertajam, Masker Penajaman Tekstur Batu Bulat, Kerutan, Etsa, Plastik, Patung Relief, Batu Transformasi Hapus Interlace, Balik Warna, Posterisasi Dialog khusus Penyesuaian Gambar membuka kotak dialog yang lebih besar: pratinjau besar yang dapat Anda zum, geser, dan putar, ditampilkan sendiri, berdampingan, atau terbelah; Sesuaikan otomatis dan pemilih titik putih dan hitam; penggeser untuk suhu, rona warna, saturasi, kecerahan, kontras, sorotan, bayangan, dan nada tengah, dengan histogram; urungkan dan ulangi di dalam dialog; serta cuplikan pengaturan untuk dibandingkan. Peningkatan Kontras menampilkan histogram dengan penanda yang dapat diseret untuk tingkat masukan dan keluaran, pipet untuk hitam dan putih, serta Sesuaikan otomatis. Kurva Nada menyunting kurva per kanal (utama, merah, hijau, biru) dalam empat gaya (kurva, lurus, tangan bebas, gamma), di atas histogram; kurva dapat disimpan dan dimuat. Warna gambar, seperti di Ganti Warna, memiliki pipet: klik pratinjau untuk mengambil warna di bawah penunjuk. Menyunting efek sebuah objek Bagian Efek di panel Properti mencantumkan efek objek yang dipilih, yang pertama diterapkan berada di atas. Setiap baris memiliki kotak centang untuk menampilkan atau menyembunyikan efek, Sunting (membuka kotak dialognya), Naikkan, Turunkan, dan Hapus. Tambah efek membuka kelompok-kelompok efek. Efek > Ratakan Efek membuat efek menjadi permanen: bitmap mempertahankan apa yang ditampilkannya, dan objek vektor menjadi bitmap. Pemilih Efek Efek > Effect Picker membuka jendela yang tetap terbuka selama Anda bekerja, dengan setiap efek sebagai gambar kecil. Ketik di kolom pencarian untuk menemukan efek, atau pilih sebuah kelompok atau Terbaru dari daftar. Bila ada yang dipilih, klik sebuah ubin untuk menerapkan efeknya. Anda juga dapat menerapkan efek sebagai lensa. Efek yang menyebar melewati tepi Efek buram dan sejenisnya dapat melampaui tepi bitmap. Dengan Bitmap > Kembangkan Bitmap > Kembangkan Bitmap Otomatis aktif (seperti bawaannya), bitmap membesar untuk memberi ruang bagi efek itu. Lihat Menyampel ulang dan meluruskan. Untuk menyimpan bitmap beserta efeknya sebagai berkas PNG, klik kanan bitmap lalu pilih Save Bitmap As.

Teks TraceDraw memiliki dua jenis teks. Teks artistik adalah satu baris, atau beberapa baris, yang ditempatkan di sebuah titik: judul, label, logo. Teks paragraf mengalir di dalam bingkai dan terlipat di tepinya: teks isi, kolom, daftar. Keduanya dapat diformat karakter demi karakter, dipasang pada jalur, dan diperiksa ejaannya. Halaman-halaman ini menjelaskan cara menambah dan memformat teks, menata paragraf, memilih font dan karakter khusus, serta memakai alat tulis.
